title: Generated spoken voice via Auritus
description:
## Purpose
As a score author, I want to generate spoken voice lines with Auritus straight into my library, so that voice layers (announcers, narration) are reproducible, carry their provenance, and sync like any other sample, with no hand-made `say` recordings.

## Not included
Singing, or generation while a score compiles. Generation happens offline into the library.

## Design
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T[text + voice] --> A[auritus.synthesize]
  A --> W[files/audio/smp_id/name.wav]
  W --> N[analyze + markup phrases]
  N --> S[Sample role=generated, alias voice/name]
  S --> C[score: clip x = voice/name.wav warp repitch]
  S --> Y[apricity sync push]
```
The sample id is `smp_` + `sha256(auritus request_key)[:20]`, so regenerating the same request is a no-op.

## Depends on
The Auritus epic auritus-9ffcc2 ("Auritus as an embeddable speech library").

## Definition of Done
- `apricity-analyze voice` generates, analyses and records a `generated` Sample with full provenance, idempotently.
- The data model and manifest schema carry `role: generated` plus a `generator` record; the contract is regenerated.
- `examples/voice-layer.apr` uses an Auritus-generated announcer.
- All specs and tests green.

comments.text: Re-scoped 2026-09-26 per the user: voice renders run on cloud GPU (AWS Batch) only, through the reusable Auritus construct (auritus-c9d582) that Apricity instantiates as its own stack. Curators only, $10/day budget, CC0 output. New tasks: B4 (instantiate) and B5 (ingest). B2 is re-scoped to the request mutation.
